summary: The 2026 Iran war (the US and Israel against Iran, since Feb 28) is in a tense pause: President Trump and Secretary of State Rubio say new strikes are unlikely or not needed while the US blockade of Iran continues, and Qatar says it sees progress in mediation. Iran denies that talks are under way and says the Strait of Hormuz stays shut to unapproved shipping until its conditions are met; attacks on tankers in and near the strait continued on Nov 10, and Iran's Revolutionary Guards said two tankers caught fire after hitting mines on Nov 11. On Nov 11 Iran's parliament speaker said the strait will never return to its pre-war status, while President Trump said the US has already won and wants a total victory. On Nov 12 Yemen's Houthis claimed attacks on Saudi oil sites, and oil rose about 3%. On Nov 13 Iran's Revolutionary Guard claimed it destroyed a US early-warning radar in Bahrain in response to an overnight strike on the Hormuz port town of Sirik; US Central Command denied it, saying US forces shot down two Iranian drones aimed at Bahrain with no injuries or damage. On Nov 14 Iran's Revolutionary Guards and navy said three oil tankers caught fire after hitting mines in and east of the strait (Reuters could not verify the claim); on Nov 13 the UN had told the Security Council at least 25 seafarers have been killed around Hormuz since February. Early on Nov 15 Bahrain said it intercepted Iranian drones aimed at US radar sites, and UKMTO reported a tanker attacked in the Gulf before entering the strait (crew safe); later on Nov 15 Iran's Revolutionary Guards warned ships the strait is closed, and a G7 statement condemned Iran's attacks and its disruption of Hormuz shipping. Brent was near US$96 on Friday, set for a second weekly fall.

status.label: Strait of Hormuz
status.note: Iran says it is closed to ships that don't coordinate with its Persian Gulf Strait Authority; the US says the main routes are controlled by the US and its regional partners. Most traffic moves through a shuttle system the US coordinates with Arab partners, with weekly volumes swinging as attacks continue (Al Jazeera).

status.label: Oil through Hormuz
status.note: About 11.6 million barrels a day over the seven days to Oct 13, about 68% of the 17.1 million pre-war baseline (Kpler, via Al Jazeera).

status.label: The war
status.note: US officials said the US carried out limited, defensive strikes on Iranian targets, including on Qeshm Island near the Strait of Hormuz on Nov 2, after Iranian surface-to-air missile threats; they said it was not a resumption of major combat (Wall Street Journal, then Reuters). Indirect talks through Qatari mediators continue with no breakthrough announced; Vice President Vance said there has been progress. On Nov 7 the US carried out further strikes on Iranian air defences on Qeshm Island, which President Trump called minor (Euronews). On Nov 8 Trump told CNN renewed attacks were highly unlikely if talks make real progress; no deal has been signed.

status.label: Brent crude
status.note: Brent fell about 1% on Monday morning, Nov 16, to near US$95 a barrel (HDFC Sky showed US$94.86, Arbiterz US$95.36) as traders weighed expectations of a coming supply surplus (CNBC).

updates.text: Iran's navy said an oil tanker caught fire after hitting a naval mine in the Strait of Hormuz (reported by ANI and Mehr News; not independently verified).
sources: ANI: Oil tanker catches fire after hitting naval mine in Hormuz, says Iranian Navy
Mehr News: Oil tanker burns after mine strike in Strait of Hormuz
Al Arabiya: Oil tanker on fire in Strait of Hormuz due to naval mine, Iran's army says

updates.text: President Trump said the US no longer needs a deal with Iran, Trading Economics reported as oil trading reopened.
Iran's Revolutionary Guards warned ships that the Strait of Hormuz is closed, after claiming a six-drone attack on a US radar at Bahrain's Al-Riffa base; Bahrain said the drones were intercepted.
A G7 statement shared by the US Embassy in Riyadh condemned Iran's attacks on its neighbours, Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia and Iran's disruption of shipping through Hormuz.

Bahrain's military said its air defenses intercepted and destroyed Iranian drones early Sunday before they reached US radar installations, its first interceptions since September; Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they launched six drones at a US radar site at Bahrain's Riffa helicopter base. No damage was confirmed.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations centre said a tanker was attacked on Sunday morning while sailing east through the Gulf before entering the Strait of Hormuz; it said the crew are accounted for and safe and named no attacker.
Iran's foreign ministry spokesman said Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi will travel to Muscat on Tuesday, Nov 17, for talks with Oman's foreign minister (IRNA, via Reuters).

Iran's Revolutionary Guards and navy said fires broke out on three oil tankers that struck mines in and east of the Strait of Hormuz, including a supertanker; the statements did not name the vessels. The US military says it has cleared the main routes of mines.

background: The war began on Feb 28, 2026 with US and Israeli strikes on Iran. An April ceasefire collapsed on July 8. The US has blockaded Iranian ports since April (reinstated in July); Iran restricts and attacks shipping through Hormuz, which carried about a fifth of the world's oil before the war.
factcheck: Checked by Claude against at least two reputable sources where possible. Statements by Iran's military, the US military (CENTCOM) or President Trump are labelled as claims, because each side's account of who controls the strait differs.
